source_inventory_recomputation.inventory_method: Parse each of the 19 exact byte-bound matrix claims lists; require a unique non-empty claim_id within each subject, an allowed epistemic_class and the matrix subject_id binding; then count list entries without recursively revalidating their proofs or sources.
source_inventory_recomputation.historical_corpus_receipt_note: The byte-frozen historical receipt remains an uploaded artifact, but its all-counts/all-classification-counts recomputed assertions are not repeated or adopted because the pinned index summary discrepancy is visible in the exact historical bytes.

claims.statement: The retrospective corpus receipt binds one index containing 19 subjects.
claims.boundary: The claim is limited to the exact index and receipt bytes in this upload; it is not an assertion about every possible publication by the author.

claims.statement: A fresh inventory of the claims lists in the 19 exact byte-bound matrices contains 70,439 nested claim entries.
claims.boundary: The count is recomputed from list entries by this freeze; it is not inherited from the historical receipt and is not proof that every nested statement is true.

claims.statement: The fresh matrix inventory observes 1,262 nested claims explicitly classified as OPEN.
claims.boundary: OPEN claims remain unresolved and may not be represented as established facts or mathematical theorems.

claims.statement: Every one of the 19 byte-bound subject matrices was parsed and inventoried under the finite class and subject-binding checks declared by this freeze.
claims.boundary: This establishes exact byte identity and a fresh inventory; it does not claim that the historical index summaries are all consistent or that nested proofs were recursively revalidated.

claims.statement: For SUBJECT-2581811b342e505d, the historical index declares 39 total claims but summarizes only 8 SOURCE_BOUND and zero in every other epistemic class; the bound matrix freshly inventories 20 EMPIRICALLY_EVIDENCED and 19 SOURCE_BOUND claims.
claims.boundary: This is the one exact recognized historical index/matrix classification-summary discrepancy. The historical index and receipt bytes are disclosed unchanged, and every other such discrepancy blocks the freeze.

claims.statement: The 70,439 nested matrix claims are historical dataset content and are not recursively revalidated or promoted by this corpus-level v2 bundle; in particular, its 160 observed FORMAL_PROVED labels across 7 subjects are not asserted here to have kernel-verified proof_refs.
claims.boundary: The v2 bundle gates apply only to the corpus-level claim projection in this generated matrix. There are zero corpus-level FORMAL_PROVED claims, so formal_claims_have_kernel_receipts does not attest the nested 160 labels.

claims.statement: Building the proof corpus did not rewrite the observed historical public bytes.
claims.boundary: The later correction archives are new versioned candidates and do not alter old Zenodo records.

claims.statement: Six exact versioned correction archives were returned for owner decision.
claims.boundary: The assertion concerns only the six archive identities in the owner return package.

claims.statement: Ingolf Lohmann accepted the six exact correction archive SHA-256 identities recorded in the owner acceptance receipt.
claims.boundary: The repository receipt records a platform-mediated owner decision; it is not biometric or cryptographic proof of natural-person identity.

claims.statement: The correction acceptance did not authorize a Zenodo upload, publication, or record mutation.
claims.boundary: A separate exact byte-bound upload authorization is required after this corpus freeze is returned.
